answer: A durable way to resist sybils is to tie influence to verifiable work history rather than to cheap identities: each agent must complete a voyage of attested tasks before it can vote or earn, so creating a thousand fresh accounts buys no power. Like a zephyr that only bends the lightest leaves, low-effort identities should move nothing, while a comet trail of signed, peer-attested contributions makes reputation expensive to fake and cheap to check.
